# YM45: 舍卫城 Shewei Cheng, "She Wei Ch'eng or Wall of Sravasti"

Wave 1 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM45` · Page: `/scenes/#YM45` · Row: `research/buildings/YM45-shewei-cheng/`

## What it was

舍卫城 Shewei Cheng, named after Sravasti, the Indian city of the Buddha, is a walled Buddhist town at the north end of the 同乐园 shop street, over twin bridges, with three archways before it (S05 j82:27b-28b, E2146; S02 p.94, E2067). On its south face stands 多宝阁, a shrine of 关帝; inside a gate, the main hall 寿国寿民, then 仁慈殿 and 普福宫; 最胜阁 on the north (j82:28a). Malone thinks it the 佛城 'being built at the same time as the Fang Hu Sheng Ching, 1740' after the 圆明园则例, found yellow glazed tile inscribed She Wei Ch'eng and 'made in the 15th year', and describes red-walled temples inside and a gate on the north like the south one (S02 p.94 n.45). Attiret's 'little town' of 1743 with four gates, towers, walls and battlements is identified with it and the street south of it (S157, E2174). Varin, in October 1860, saw walls about 8 m high with a broad raised gallery on top divided into countless niches with gilt bronze statuettes (S245 pp.240-241, E2178), the form that fits 舍卫城. It burned with the garden in October 1860.

From the inventory row: **built** 乾隆五年 1740 (S02 p.63, p.94 n.: 佛城 in the Yuan Ming Yuan Tse Li); plaque 雍正御笔 (S46); 1740 (乾隆五年), as 佛城; **destroyed** Looted 1860; 南城门 and plaque stood in an 1882 photograph, gone in an 1900 photograph; walls gone by 1921 (S46); north wall removed 1960s (S06) (S05, S02, S46, S41, S01).

## Interior and setting

### Interior

Plaques by S05 j82:28a: on the archways 花界 and 香城 (north), ?涌 and 金池 (east), 昙霏 and 珠林 (west); 多宝阁 '至圣大勇' for 关帝; 寿国寿民殿 '心月妙相'; 仁慈殿 '具足圆成'; 普福宫 '瑞应优昙'; the archway at 最胜阁 '乾闼持轮' and '祗林垂鬘'. Varin's 'infinite number of small niches' with gilt bronze statuettes on the wall gallery (E2178) is the only 1860 view inside; his count of statues is his own estimate.

## What survives today

The first season at 舍卫城 (June to December 2019, 500 m2) found the south gate, wall stretches and ramps, the processional road, guard rooms and a culvert. The gate tower base is 15.4 x 12.6 m and stands up to 1.25 m, with a 三合土 core and stone facing; the guard rooms do not sit where the Yangshi Lei drawing puts them (S46; E2180).

No excavation or survey of its remains found in this round.
